#!/bin/sh # The evaluation's render command (see PROTOCOL.md). exec node /opt/render/render.mjs "$@" /opt/render: node_modules package-lock.json package.json render.mjs /opt/render/node_modules/time-i-gram: LICENSE README.md dist package.json # time-i-gram **A grammar for interactive visualization of time-based data.** time-i-gram extends [Gosling.js](https://github.com/gosling-lang/gosling.js) with a temporal field type, time-aware data sources (`csv-time`, `json-time`), a time axis, time coordinate systems (calendar periods such as "week of the year" and offsets relative to an event), calendar units with aggregation, and time transforms. A visualization is a JSON spec; `embed` renders it, with zooming, brushing and linked views. This package is a single self-contained ES module: React, PixiJS, HiGlass and their CSS are bundled, so there is nothing else to install. The grammar, the editor with examples and the source code: https://github.com/vanessastoiber/time-i-gram ## Install From a CDN, nothing to install: ```js import { embed } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/time-i-gram@0.1.0/dist/index.js'; ``` With a bundler (Vite, esbuild, webpack, ...): ```bash npm install time-i-gram ``` ```js import { embed } from 'time-i-gram'; ``` ## Usage in a plain HTML page ```html
``` `embed(element, spec, options?)` returns a promise of the visualization's API (zoom to a range, subscribe to events, export images). ## Usage in Observable In an [Observable notebook](https://observablehq.com), `embed(spec)` returns an element that the cell displays: ```js embed = (await import('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/time-i-gram@0.1.0/dist/index.js')).embed ``` ```js embed({ /* a time-i-gram spec */ }) ``` In [Observable Framework](https://observablehq.com/framework/): ```js import { embed } from 'npm:time-i-gram@0.1.0'; display(await embed({ /* a time-i-gram spec */ })); ``` ## TypeScript The package includes types for `embed` and for specs: ```ts import { embed, type GoslingSpec } from 'time-i-gram'; ``` ## Citation If you use time-i-gram in your research, please cite: > V. Stoiber, D. Chacón-Ramírez, N. Gehlenborg, W. Aigner, and M. Streit, "time-i-gram: A Grammar for > Interactive Visualization of Time-based Data," Center for Open Science (preprint), 2026. > doi: [10.31219/osf.io/m9ubg_v2](https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/m9ubg_v2) ```bibtex @article{Stoiber2026, title = {time-i-gram: A Grammar for Interactive Visualization of Time-based Data}, doi = {10.31219/osf.io/m9ubg_v2}, url = {https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/m9ubg_v2}, publisher = {Center for Open Science}, author = {Stoiber, Vanessa and Chacón-Ramírez, Denisse and Gehlenborg, Nils and Aigner, Wolfgang and Streit, Marc}, year = {2026}, month = aug } ``` ## License MIT. time-i-gram is built on [Gosling.js](https://github.com/gosling-lang/gosling.js) (MIT) and [HiGlass](https://github.com/higlass/higlass) (MIT).

content.text:
I've built `/work/spec.json`, a time-i-gram spec showing five years of Wien Hohe Warte temperature with a linked detail view down to single 10-minute readings. It renders with status OK. The renderer also logs 16 warnings ("unknown data type: undefined", "No dataConfig children…"); I did not trace where they come from. The render command only produces a static image, so I could not test brushing, zooming or tooltips. Those rely on time-i-gram's built-in linking and zoom rules, set up the same way as the project's own Beijing air-quality example.

What the figure shows:
- **Overview:** the daily mean temperature from 2020 to 2024, with year labels, and a brush that controls the detail view.
- **Detail, temperature:** opens on 15–17 July 2024 and shows every 10-minute reading. Zoomed out, it switches to hourly means once the shown span is 4 days or more, and to daily means from 60 days. Hovering a point shows its UTC time and value.
- **Detail, precipitation:** bars in their own track, aligned with temperature. They are summed with the same hourly/daily switching.
- **Caption:** "Temperature follows a strong annual cycle with a daily cycle on top; rain comes in short bursts."

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.json
requirements:
  R1: done - overview of daily mean tl over 2020–2024, axis labelled by year
  R2: done - detail shows raw 10-min readings when span < 4 days (hourly means < 60 days, daily above)
  R3: done - brush in overview linked to the detail view; only static render checked
  R4: done - rr bar track below tl in the detail view, same linked x axis
  R5: done - overview axis shows years; detail axis shows days and hh:mm, adapting to zoom
  R6: done - full CSV loaded from the URL via csv-time; aggregation only inside the spec
  R7: done - title, one-sentence caption, °C / mm per 10 min / UTC in track and axis titles
assumptions:
  - Overview aggregates tl to daily means
  - Detail opens on 15–17 July 2024 so single readings are visible at start; the period was picked by hand, not computed
  - Temperature y range fixed at -15 to 40 °C so values below zero are not cut off (auto scale started at 0)
  - Precipitation is summed per hour/day when zoomed out; the axis is titled "Precip. (mm)", and the track title says it is mm per 10 min at full detail
limitations:
  - The overview year axis has no month labels; months appear only in the detail view
  - "UTC" is in track titles, not as an x-axis title
  - At 4–60 day spans the detail shows hourly means, not single readings
  - Loading the ~263k-row CSV takes roughly 20 s before the figure appears
  - The renderer logs 16 warnings ("unknown data type: undefined", "No dataConfig children…"); cause not traced, render still OK
  - The 0 °C tick label on the overview y axis overlaps the line slightly
```

- **Detail, precipitation:** bars in their own track, aligned with temperature. They are summed with the same hourly/daily switching.
- **Caption:** "Temperature follows a strong annual cycle with a daily cycle on top; rain comes in short bursts."
